library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(janitor)
library(dbplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(patchwork)
library(ggcube)
library(geometry)
library(gganimate)
library(plotly)
# Add any other libraries here
# load your data 

df = read.csv("data/SeoulBikeData.csv", fileEncoding = "latin1") %>% clean_names() %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date, format = "%d/%m/%Y"))
df_seasons_mean <- df %>% 
  group_by(seasons) %>% 
  summarise(mean_hourly_bike_count = mean(rented_bike_count, na.rm= TRUE))

df_date_mean <- df %>% 
  group_by(date) %>% 
  summarise(mean_hourly_bike_count = mean(rented_bike_count, na.rm= TRUE))

df_hour_mean <- df %>% 
  group_by(hour) %>% 
  summarise(mean_hourly_bike_count = mean(rented_bike_count, na.rm= TRUE))


df_temp_mean <- df %>% 
  mutate(temp_grp = factor(
    case_when(
      temperature_c <= -10 ~ "Extremely low",
      temperature_c >= -10 & temperature_c < 0 ~ "Very low",
      temperature_c >= 0 & temperature_c < 10 ~ "Low",
      temperature_c >= 10 & temperature_c < 20 ~ "Mid",
      temperature_c >= 20 & temperature_c < 30 ~ "High",
      temperature_c >= 30 & temperature_c < 40 ~ "Very high",
      TRUE ~ "Extremely high" 
      ), 
    level = c("Extremely low", 
              "Very low", 
              "Low", 
              "Mid", 
              "High", 
              "Very high", 
              "Extremely high"))) %>% 
  group_by(temp_grp) %>% 
  summarise(mean_bike_count = mean(rented_bike_count, na.rm= TRUE))
trialdf1 = df %>% select(-functioning_day, -holiday) %>% group_by(hour, seasons) %>% 
  summarise(
    Mean = mean(rented_bike_count, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
## `summarise()` has regrouped the output.
## ℹ Summaries were computed grouped by hour and seasons.
## ℹ Output is grouped by hour.
## ℹ Use `summarise(.groups = "drop_last")` to silence this message.
## ℹ Use `summarise(.by = c(hour, seasons))` for per-operation grouping
##   (`?dplyr::dplyr_by`) instead.
trialdf2 = df %>% select(-functioning_day, -holiday) %>% group_by(hour, seasons) %>% 
  summarise(
    m = mean(temperature_c, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
## `summarise()` has regrouped the output.
## ℹ Summaries were computed grouped by hour and seasons.
## ℹ Output is grouped by hour.
## ℹ Use `summarise(.groups = "drop_last")` to silence this message.
## ℹ Use `summarise(.by = c(hour, seasons))` for per-operation grouping
##   (`?dplyr::dplyr_by`) instead.
coeff = 0.01

ggplot() +
  geom_bar(data = trialdf1, aes(x = hour, y = Mean), stat = "identity", alpha = 0.7, fill = "lightblue") +
  geom_point(data = trialdf2, aes(x = hour, y = m/coeff), size = 2, colour = "grey") +
  facet_wrap(~ seasons) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Mean Rented Bike Count",
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~.*coeff, name="Mean Temperature (C)")
  )+
  theme(
    axis.title.y = element_text(color = "lightblue", size=13),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = "grey", size=13)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Hour",
    title = "Effect Temperature has on Rented Bike Count (by hours of the day)"
  ) 

trialdf3 = df %>% select(-functioning_day, -holiday) %>% group_by(hour, seasons) %>% 
  summarise(
    mean_bike_count = mean(rented_bike_count, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
## `summarise()` has regrouped the output.
## ℹ Summaries were computed grouped by hour and seasons.

    mean_temperature = mean(temperature_c, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
## `summarise()` has regrouped the output.

ggplot(data = trialdf5, 
       mapping = aes(x = mean_bike_count, y = mean_temperature, colour = seasons)) +
geom_point() + 
  facet_wrap(~ seasons) +
labs(title = "Correlation Between Temperature and Bike Demand",

       y = "Mean Temperature (°C)",
     colour= "Seasons")

trialdf6 <- df %>% 
  select(date, rented_bike_count, temperature_c, seasons) %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarise(day_bike_count = sum(rented_bike_count), 
            mean_day_temp_c = mean(temperature_c))


coeff <- 0.001

ggplot(trialdf6, aes(x = date)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = day_bike_count), 
             colour = "tomato", size = 0.6) + 
  geom_smooth(aes(y = day_bike_count), 
              colour = "tomato", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(aes(y = mean_day_temp_c/ coeff), 
             colour = "cornflowerblue", size = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(aes(y = mean_day_temp_c/ coeff), 
              colour = "cornflowerblue", linewidth = 0.6) +
  labs(x = "Date",
       title = "Correlation Between Number of Rented Bikes and Temperature") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Number of Rented Bikes",
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~.*coeff, name="Temperature (in degrees celsius)")
  )+
  theme(
    axis.title.y = element_text(color = "tomato", size = 13),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = "cornflowerblue", size = 13)
  ) 
## `geom_smooth()` using method = 'loess' and formula = 'y ~ x'
## `geom_smooth()` using method = 'loess' and formula = 'y ~ x'

ggplot(data = trialdf14,
       mapping = aes(x = mean_day_temp_c, y = day_bike_count))+
  geom_point(colour = "lightblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "orange", se = FALSE)+
  labs(
    y ="daily bike count",
    x ="mean daily temperature (c)",
    title = "Linear relationship between daily bike demand and temperature"
  )+
  theme_bw()
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

linear_reg()%>%
  set_engine("lm") %>%
   fit(day_bike_count ~ mean_day_temp_c, data = trialdf14) %>%
  tidy()
## # A tibble: 2 × 5
##   term            estimate std.error statistic  p.value
##   <chr>              <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>
## 1 (Intercept)        8907.     576.       15.5 7.83e-42
## 2 mean_day_temp_c     621.      33.3      18.7 5.46e-55
bike_temp_fit <- linear_reg() %>% 
  set_engine("lm") %>%
   fit(day_bike_count ~ mean_day_temp_c, data = trialdf14)

 bike_temp_fit_aug <- augment(bike_temp_fit$fit)

ggplot(bike_temp_fit_aug, mapping = aes(x = .fitted, y = .resid)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "gray", lty = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Predicted bike demand", y = "Residuals", title = "Residuals for Predicted Bike Demand from Mean Daily Temperature") +
  theme_bw()

glance(bike_temp_fit)
## # A tibble: 1 × 12
##   r.squared adj.r.squared sigma statistic  p.value    df logLik   AIC   BIC
##       <dbl>         <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
## 1     0.490         0.488 7338.      348. 5.46e-55     1 -3766. 7537. 7549.
## # ℹ 3 more variables: deviance <dbl>, df.residual <int>, nobs <int>

Comments about model1: from graph linear relationship appears weak from residual plot we can see as predicted bike demand increases the residuals increase as well which is a pattern meaning the model is not a good fit residuals are quite significant, upto almost -20,000 meaning the accuracy is low from the glance function, r squared is 0.488 which is 48.8% so mean temperature explains 48.8% of variance in the daily bike demand which is decent for the model. formula for expected bike demand: daily bike demand = 8906.84 + 621.26 ✕ mean daily temp intercept is 8906.84 which is the expected demand for when mean daily temperature is 0, it is not exactly possible as bike demand cannot be in decimals but an approximate demand of 8907 is possible. the slope is 621.26 which means on average as the mean daily temperature increases by one degree celsius, we expect the demand of bikes for that day to increase by 621.26. Again while it is not possible to have an increase in bikes in decimals, an approximate increase of 621 is possible. ggplot(data = trialdf14,
       mapping = aes(x = mean_day_temp_c, y = mean_day_humidity, z = day_bike_count))+
  geom_point_3d(colour = "lightblue") +
  labs(
    y ="mean daily humidity (%)",
    x ="mean daily temperature (c)",
    z = "daily bike count",
    title = "Linear relationship between daily bike demand, mean daily humidity and mean daily temperature"
  )+
  theme_bw() + coord_3d()

linear_reg()%>%
  set_engine("lm") %>%
   fit(day_bike_count ~ mean_day_humidity, data = trialdf14) %>%
  tidy()

## # A tibble: 2 × 5

linear_reg()%>%

bike_temp_humid_fit <- linear_reg() %>% 
  set_engine("lm") %>%
   fit(day_bike_count ~ mean_day_humidity + mean_day_temp_c, data = trialdf14)

 bike_temp_humid_fit_aug <- augment(bike_temp_humid_fit$fit)

ggplot(bike_temp_humid_fit_aug, mapping = aes(x = .fitted, y = .resid)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "gray", lty = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Predicted bike demand", y = "Residuals", title = "Residuals for Predicted Bike Demand from Mean Daily Temperature and Mean Daily Humidity") +
  theme_bw()

glance(bike_temp_humid_fit)

bike_sun_df <- trialdf15 %>%
  group_by(date, hours_of_sunlight) %>%
  summarise(day_bike_count = sum(rented_bike_count))
## `summarise()` has regrouped the output.
## ℹ Summaries were computed grouped by date and hours_of_sunlight.
## ℹ Output is grouped by date.
## ℹ Use `summarise(.groups = "drop_last")` to silence this message.
## ℹ Use `summarise(.by = c(date, hours_of_sunlight))` for per-operation grouping
##   (`?dplyr::dplyr_by`) instead.
bike_sun_fit <- linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm") %>%
  fit(day_bike_count ~ hours_of_sunlight, data = bike_sun_df)
  
tidy(bike_sun_fit)
## # A tibble: 2 × 5

ggplot(data = bike_sun_df, mapping = aes(x = hours_of_sunlight, y = day_bike_count)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.5, colour = "gold") +
geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "skyblue", se = FALSE) +
  labs( x = "Hours of Sunlight",
        y = "Total Bike Count for a Day",
        title = "Linear model for daily bike count from hours of sunlight") +
  theme_bw()

formula : bikedemand = -25386.97 + 3461.56*sunlighthours The formula for this linear model tells us that, on average, for every hour increase in sunlight in a day, the total bike demand increases by 3461.56 for that day. The decimals are not possible, however we can round this up for the model to give a reasonable predicted on change in bike demand with sunlight hours. On the other hand, the model predicts a value of -25386.97 for bike demand when there are 0 hours of sunlight in a day, which is not possible and tells us the model may not be suitable. The adjusted R^2 value for this model tells us that around 47% of the variability in response is explained by the linear model.

df_bike_cat <- df %>% 
  mutate(bike_grp = factor(
    case_when(
      rented_bike_count <= 400 ~ "0-400",
      rented_bike_count <= 800 ~ "401-800",
      rented_bike_count <= 1200 ~ "801-1200",
      rented_bike_count <= 1600 ~ "1201-1600",
      rented_bike_count <= 2000 ~ "1601-2000",
      rented_bike_count <= 2400 ~ "2001-2400",
      rented_bike_count > 2400 ~ "Greater than 2400"
    ),
    levels = c("0-400",
               "401-800",
               "801-1200",
               "1201-1600",
               "1601-2000",
               "2001-2400",
               "Greater than 2400"),
    ordered = TRUE
  ))

set.seed(1234)

bike_split <- initial_split(df_bike_cat)
bike_train <- training(bike_split)
bike_test <- testing(bike_split)

bike_rec <- recipe(bike_grp ~ temperature_c, 
                   data = bike_train)

bike_mod <- multinom_reg() %>% 
  set_engine("nnet") 

bike_wflow <- workflow() %>% 
  add_model(bike_mod) %>% 
  add_recipe(bike_rec)

bike_fit <- bike_wflow %>% 
  fit(data = bike_train)

bike_pred <- predict(bike_fit, bike_test, type = "prob") %>% 
  bind_cols(predict(bike_fit, bike_test, type = "class")) %>%
  bind_cols(bike_test %>% select(bike_grp, temperature_c))


bike_pred %>%
  roc_auc(
    truth = bike_grp,
    `.pred_0-400`,
    `.pred_401-800`,
    `.pred_801-1200`,
    `.pred_1201-1600`,
    `.pred_1601-2000`,
    `.pred_2001-2400`,
    `.pred_Greater than 2400`,
    estimator = "hand_till"
  )
## # A tibble: 1 × 3
##   .metric .estimator .estimate
##   <chr>   <chr>          <dbl>
## 1 roc_auc hand_till      0.611
bike_pred %>%
  roc_curve(
    truth = bike_grp,
    `.pred_0-400`,
    `.pred_401-800`,
    `.pred_801-1200`,
    `.pred_1201-1600`,
    `.pred_1601-2000`,
    `.pred_2001-2400`,
    `.pred_Greater than 2400`,
    estimator = "hand_till"
  ) %>%
  autoplot()
